Somos K2-315b (nombre del planeta pi), estudiantes de 1° de MatInf.  Estamos aquí para ver qué podemos hacer, sin presión.

We are K2-315b (name of the planet pi), first-year Mathematics and Computer Engineering students. We are here to see what we can achieve putting our minds together.
summary: Our proyect is a demo of a game designed to give young children a taste of what would it be like going to Mars. On this game the problem of the solar radiation is solved by using  fungi found in Chernobyl that uses the radiation as a source of energy. The player has to take care of them among other tasks.
details:
Our proyect consists of a game that will help kids understand how a spacial base located in Mars works and some of the tasks that the astronauts have to do inside them. Our goal is to inspire them to follow the path of an astronaut and maybe have them solve some of the problems we have in the future.

We have used the game engine Godot along with its integrated language (GDScript) to code all of it. As for the graphics and designs of the game, we have used the web Piskel to draw all of it giving it a very modern and appealing pixel art aesthetic.

We considered the use of a fungi called Cladosporium sphaerospermum to absorb radiation, this specimen has been found in Chernobyl getting energy from the solar radiation, so we thought it could block the radiation from the Sun, as the atmosphere in Mars is really thin and it lets the solar radiation through. Also, thoughout the mission the player has to cultivate different crops including lettuce, which has some research done about it.

We decided not to use AI to create the project. Three of the four team members are beginners in programming, and we believe AI is fine to use only when you truly understand what it is telling you. So instead, we chose to make the most of our own abilities and divided the work according to each person’s strengths. Part of the team drew the character and the scenery by hand, one member researched the information about life on a Mars station, and the teammate with the most programming experience wrote the code. The result is a game that is entirely the work of our team, and every part of it is something we understand and can explain

Creativity also shaped our visual style. We chose a simple, colourful pixel-art look because the game is aimed at children. A simple appearance means that it will not put them off with unnecessary complexity, and the game is easy to understand from the first minute.

Fun Fact: The astronaut that is controlled by the player is that small because it's supposed to resemble a little child.
